current_activity: first major attack: Operation Clipper toward Geilenkirchen under British operational control
notes: Event date: 18 November 1944 (Siegfried p545: the 84th Division was to make the main effort by passing through the 102nd Division's narrow sector in the early morning of 18 November, two days after the Roer offensive began, with the division "attached for operations to the British but still tied for other purposes to the XIII Corps"). Siegfried p565 names the operation Clipper. Event definition: the 84th Division, newly arrived, attacks toward Geilenkirchen alongside the British 43rd Division (p545). The row uses the planned date of p545; the execution date was not read in a separate page. Relationship: British XXX Corps and British Second Army operational_control from 11 to 22 November (CMH table); Ninth Army and 12th Army Group assigned. Location: Division command post at Eygelshoven on 16 November (atlas), two days earlier. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Eygelshoven. Event support: moderate (planned date; execution not separately read). Location support: moderate (two days before).

current_activity: leaves Ninth Army's Roer front for First Army; temporarily attached to XVIII Airborne Corps, entering Marche that night
notes: Event date: 20 December 1944 (Ardennes p426: Bolling received orders on the night of the 19th to make ready for relief by the 102nd Division, and at noon on 20 December his leading regimental combat team, the 334th, was on the road to Belgium; "Temporarily attached to the XVIII Airborne Corps"; p427: two hours before midnight on 20 December the leading troops entered Marche; p429: the division command post at Marche on 21 December. The CMH table lists XVIII Airborne Corps and then VII Corps on 20 December). Event definition: Bradley orders the 84th to leave the Ninth Army and come in on Ridgway's flank; the division moves 75 miles from the Geilenkirchen sector to Marche and is the nucleus of the new VII Corps front, which Collins assembles from the early morning of the 21st (p426). Relationship: XVIII Airborne Corps temporarily (p426), then VII Corps (CMH table, same date); First Army attached; Ninth Army and 12th Army Group assigned; British 21st Army Group attached (CMH table). Location: Division command post at Marche on 21 December (atlas and p429), one day after the row date; the leading troops reached Marche late on the 20th. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Marche-en-Famenne. Event support: high (Green Book narrative with times). Location support: moderate (one day later; the command post may have opened on the night of the 20th).
